Okay, so the user wants me to generate a support_resistance trading strategy using specific market data and requirements. Let me break this down step by step.

First, I see that the learning insights include common indicators like RSI, MA, and MACD, but the requirements specify using Money Flow Index (MFI) and MACD. So I'll focus on those two.

The strategy needs to be of type support_resistance, so I'll incorporate rules based on identifying support and resistance levels. I'll use MFI to spot divergences, which can indicate potential trend reversals. MACD will help confirm these signals with crossovers.

For risk management, the Kelly Criterion is required. I remember the formula involves the win rate and the ratio of wins to losses. I'll calculate the optimal position size based on the user's provided performance metrics, specifically the win rate and the Sharpe Ratio.

Entry rules should include buying when MFI shows a bullish divergence and MACD line crosses above the signal line. Selling will be the opposite: bearish divergence and MACD crossover below. I'll also set stop-loss and take-profit levels based on volatility and recent high/lows to manage risk effectively.

Exit rules will use the same indicators for confirmation. I'll also include trailing stops to lock in profits as the price moves favorably.

In the code, I'll structure it to calculate MFI and MACD, identify divergences, and execute trades based on the defined rules. Position sizing will use the Kelly Criterion to determine the fraction of capital to invest. I'll make sure to include stop-loss and take-profit levels, adjusting them as needed for market volatility.

I should also consider the market data summary: the price range and volatility will influence how I set the stop-loss and take-profit levels. Since volatility is moderate, I'll set reasonable multipliers to avoid getting stopped out too early.

Finally, I'll format everything into JSON as specified, ensuring each section is clear and concise. I'll explain the reasoning behind each part so the user understands the strategy's logic.

```json
{
  "strategy_type": "support_resistance",
  "indicators": [
    {
      "name": "Money Flow Index (MFI)",
      "parameters": {
        "period": 14
      }
    },
    {
      "name": "MACD",
      "parameters": {
        "fast_ema": 12,
        "slow_ema": 26,
        "signal_ema": 9
      }
    }
  ],
  "entry_rules": {
    "long_entry": [
      "MFI shows bullish divergence (price makes a lower low while MFI makes a higher low)",
      "MACD line crosses above the signal line"
    ],
    "short_entry": [
      "MFI shows bearish divergence (price makes a higher high while MFI makes a lower high)",
      "MACD line crosses below the signal line"
    ]
  },
  "exit_rules": {
    "long_exit": [
      "MFI reaches overbought level (above 80) and starts to decline",
      "MACD line crosses below the signal line",
      "Price hits the take-profit level"
    ],
    "short_exit": [
      "MFI reaches oversold level (below 20) and starts to rise",
      "MACD line crosses above the signal line",
      "Price hits the take-profit level"
    ]
  },
  "risk_management": {
    "method": "kelly_criterion",
    "parameters": {
      "win_rate": 0.4,
      "risk_reward_ratio": 2,
      "volatility": 0.0277
    },
    "position_sizing": {
      "fraction": 0.2,
      "stop_loss": {
        "type": "volatility-based",
        "multiplier": 1
      },
      "take_profit": {
        "type": "fixed_ratio",
        "ratio": 2
      }
    }
  },
  "code": "import pandas as pd\nimport numpy as np\n\n# Calculate MFI\ndef calculate_mfi(data, period=14):\n    df = data.copy()\n    df['typ'] = (df['close'] * df['volume')\n    df['money_flow'] = df['typ'].rolling(window=period).sum()\n    df['high_low_avg'] = (df['high'] + df['low']) / 2\n    df['mfi'] = df['money_flow'] / df['high_low_avg'].rolling(window=period).sum()\n    df['mfi'] = 100 - (100 / (1 + df['mfi']))\n    return df\n\n# Calculate MACD\ndef calculate_macd(data, fast_ema=12, slow_ema=26, signal_ema=9):\n    df = data.copy()\n    df['ema_fast'] = df['close'].ewm(span=fast_ema, adjust=False).mean()\n    df['ema_slow'] = df['close'].ewm(span=slow_ema, adjust=False).mean()\n    df['macd'] = df['ema_fast'] - df['ema_slow']\n    df['signal'] = df['macd'].ewm(span=signal_ema, adjust=False).mean()\n    return df\n\n# Kelly Criterion\ndef calculate_kelly_fraction(win_rate, risk_reward_ratio):\n    return (win_rate * risk_reward_ratio - (1 - win_rate)) / (risk_reward_ratio)\n\n# Strategy Logic\ndef strategy(data):\n    df = calculate_mfi(data)\n    df = calculate_macd(df)\n    df['position'] = 0\n    df['stop_loss'] = 0\n    df['take_profit'] = 0\n    \n    for i in range(len(df)):\n        if df['mfi'][i] < 20 and df['macd'][i] > df['signal'][i]:\n            df.loc[i, 'position'] = 1\n            df.loc[i, 'stop_loss'] = df['low'][i] * (1 - 0.02)\n            df.loc[i, 'take_profit'] = df['high'][i] * (1 + 0.04)\n        elif df['mfi'][i] > 80 and df['macd'][i] < df['signal'][i]:\n            df.loc[i, 'position'] = -1\n            df.loc[i, 'stop_loss'] = df['high'][i] * (1 + 0.02)\n            df.loc[i, 'take_profit'] = df['low'][i] * (1 - 0.04)\n    return df"
}
```
